question: Why can almost no bacteria grow in saturated brine, though it is mostly water?
answer: Because its water is held, not free. Microbes need water they can take up, measured as water activity, 0 to 1. Most bacteria stop below about 0.91, Staphylococcus aureus near 0.86; saturated brine sits near 0.75, so cells lose water instead of gaining it. Only salt-loving microbes thrive, and they turn salt ponds pink.
move: Ask how much of a resource is usable, not how much is present.
reference: Jay, Loessner & Golden, Modern Food Microbiology, 7th edition, Springer, 2005
